quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When braking on a surface with low traction, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes faster than normal.
Apply the brakes slower and gentler than normal.
Not use the rear brake.
Not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes slower and gentler than normal.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with low traction, use gentle brake pressure. This helps you slow down or stop safely without losing control.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only on slippery roads.
Is not as strong as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake and is safe when used properly.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can stop other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding on the left side of the lane.
Riding in the center of the lane.
Looking angry at drivers who move into your lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to prevent other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black text. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must complete the pass while staying at or below the speed limit.
You may finish a pass in a no-passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You may drive faster than the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass while staying at or below the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Move side to side across the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back too soon.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Follow vehicles more closely.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Ride faster than usual.
Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances. Slow down and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you.
Is not worth the effort.
Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
Means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will properly yield to you. Always drive defensively.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Clean the mirrors.
Check that the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: One benefit of doing regular maintenance on your motorcycle is that:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance takes very little time.
Maintenance is inexpensive.
Maintenance checks can help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: Regular maintenance and inspections help your motorcycle run like new for many years.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement provides the best traction for your tires.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it difficult to see.
Use only one lane position.
Reduce your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance at night. Use your high beam when there is no oncoming traffic. Be ready to change your lane position if road conditions change.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury in a crash, do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Wear an approved helmet.
Wear face or eye protection.
Wear protective clothing.
Have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing to reduce injury risk. A windshield is not necessary for protection.

questions.question: When riding with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar.
questions.explanation: The passenger should sit in the sidecar and keep their hands inside at all times.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely on your mirrors to show you all of your surroundings.
Point in the direction of the lane change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Brake suddenly.
Steer in a weaving pattern.
Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the leftmost portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and go straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging to stop the weave will only make it worse.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what brakes should you use?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Sharply squeeze the front brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This habit helps you stop quickly when needed.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the part of the lane that makes other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to avoid oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly so your headlight is spotted better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of the lane that makes other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle so other drivers see you as early as possible. For example, when approaching a blind corner on your right, stay in the left part of your lane.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Lean as the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Sit directly behind the operator and lean when they lean. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator.

questions.question: Which of these provides good protection while riding?

options.text: A jacket that leaves your arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below your ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear boots or sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles with low heels. Leather gloves protect your hands and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Help you avoid hazards on the road.
Give you an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position affects many safety factors. It should keep you out of blind spots, help you see and be seen, help you avoid road hazards, protect you from wind blasts, and give you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers do not try to share your lane.

questions.question: Where do motorcycles and other vehicles have the greatest chance of conflict?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk for conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic is at intersections. Stay alert at places where another vehicle might cross your path.

questions.question: At an intersection, how can you increase your chances of being seen?

options.text: Turn your headlight off.
Ride with your headlight on.
Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on is the best way to help others see you at an intersection. Always keep your headlight on while your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where drivers don't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where drivers don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice it. Flash your brake light before slowing down where drivers may not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distance?

options.text: Pairs
Staggered formation
Single-file line
Passing formation

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way to keep riders close while maintaining safe distance. Use single-file lines when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving highways. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.
